paragraphs: Okay, friend, this one is heavy, so let me say the big thing plain. Paul says God has made Himself clear in everything He made: "His eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly seen, being understood from His workmanship, so that men are without excuse." (Romans 1:20) The problem was never that God hid. The problem is that people "suppress the truth by their wickedness." (Romans 1:18)

Look at how the slide goes: they knew God, but they "neither glorified Him as God nor gave thanks to Him." (Romans 1:21) Then their thinking turned futile and their hearts darkened, and three times Paul says God gave them over (Romans 1:24, 26, 28). I think that is sobering, because when people keep pushing God away, He can let them have what they chose. Then Paul ends with people who know God's righteous decree and still "approve of those who practice them." (Romans 1:32)

So what do I do with that, baker? I don't read it to point fingers, I read it as a check on my own heart, because Paul names two things these people didn't do: glorify God and thank Him. Paul wrote this to believers who had just heard that the gospel is "the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes." (Romans 1:16) So give God the glory and the thanks today, and the teaching isn't over, because Paul is still building his case.
